title: A micro game
subtitle: in one file.
summary: A 30-second click game on a canvas: typed-array state, a fixed step, pooled effects, a change-only HUD and Recall on Escape.
lead: This guide builds a whole game in about 80 lines: squares drift around a canvas, a click pops the ones under the pointer, and a score and a 30-second clock count on the page. It uses the kernel and four bricks, keeps every rule of the [contract](/docs/contract/), and gives the page back on Escape.

body.text: A root element holds the canvas and the readouts. The engine pauses when this root scrolls off screen, and the HUD looks up its readouts inside it.

items.title: State in typed arrays
items.body: Positions, velocities, the score and the clock live in `Float64Array`s made once. The step reads and writes numbers only, so nothing is allocated while it plays (contract rule 3).

items.title: `read` measures, `step` simulates
items.body: The canvas's CSS width is read in `read`, once a frame. The step moves the squares at a fixed 60 Hz and checks the click with `circles` from `fizlet/collide`: no layout reads (rule 4).

items.title: One click, one step
items.body: `input.pointer.hit` is true in exactly one fixed step after a click, even if that step comes frames later, so a click never pops twice or gets lost.

items.title: Events, not callbacks
items.body: A pop goes on the event ring in the step; `render` reads the ring and plays `fx.blast`. The effects are pooled (`cap: 240`): a full pool refuses particles and counts them, it never grows.

items.title: A HUD that writes only changes
items.body: `hud(e, board).num(…)` compares each readout after rounding to what it shows and writes the page only when that changed, through the ledger. The clock is a slot in a typed array, so it never boxes a number.

items.title: Escape is Recall
items.body: `e.destroy()` removes every listener (the keydown listener goes with `e.signal`) and undoes every page change the engine made.

body.text: Each import is its own module with its own budget. Measured on this build, gzip, each with everything it imports: the kernel {size:fizlet (kernel)}, `fizlet/input` {size:fizlet/input}, `fizlet/fx` {size:fizlet/fx}, `fizlet/hud` {size:fizlet/hud}, `fizlet/collide` {size:fizlet/collide}. The kernel is shared, so a bundle of all five is smaller than their sum; bundle and gzip your build to see your exact number.

items.title: Sound
items.body: `sound(e, { cues: { pop: "boom" } })` plays a synth cue for every `pop` on the ring: no audio files, at most 8 voices. [fizlet/sound](/bricks/sound.html).

items.title: A start screen and a clock
items.body: `match(e, root, { count: 3, seconds: 30 })` adds PRESS START, a 3-2-1, pause on Escape or P, and a result with REMATCH. [fizlet/match](/bricks/match.html).

items.title: Touch controls
items.body: `pad(e, input, { scheme: "stick" })` adds an on-screen stick and arcade keys that drive the same intents. [fizlet/pad](/bricks/pad.html).

items.title: The page as the board
items.body: `boardPage(e)` turns the page's own letters into terrain and its buttons into targets, and Recall gives every one back. [fizlet/board-page](/bricks/board-page.html).
